classification.difficultyReason: Use the given ratio and sign conditions to select the correct square-root sign, recover a missing ratio with the Pythagorean identity, and form a quotient; part (c) also requires first converting cosecant to sine.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If $\sin\alpha=\frac35$ and $90^\circ<\alpha<180^\circ$, find the value of $\cos\alpha$ and $\tan\alpha$.

answer.worked: In quadrant II, cosine is negative. $$\begin{align*}\cos\alpha&=-\sqrt{1-\sin^2\alpha}\\\cos\alpha&=-\sqrt{1-\left(\frac35\right)^2}\\\cos\alpha&=-\frac45\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha}\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{3/5}{-4/5}\\\tan\alpha&=-\frac34\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If $\cos\alpha=-\frac45$ and $\sin\alpha<0$, find the exact value of $\tan\alpha$.

answer.worked: Both sine and cosine are negative, so $\alpha$ lies in quadrant III. $$\begin{align*}\sin\alpha&=-\sqrt{1-\cos^2\alpha}\\\sin\alpha&=-\sqrt{1-\left(-\frac45\right)^2}\\\sin\alpha&=-\frac35\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha}\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{-3/5}{-4/5}\\\tan\alpha&=\frac34\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\sin\alpha&=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosec}\alpha}\\\sin\alpha&=-\frac5{13}\end{align*}$$Sine is negative and cosine is positive, so $\alpha$ lies in quadrant IV. $$\begin{align*}\cos\alpha&=\sqrt{1-\left(-\frac5{13}\right)^2}\\\cos\alpha&=\frac{12}{13}\\\cot\alpha&=\frac{\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}\\\cot\alpha&=\frac{12/13}{-5/13}\\\cot\alpha&=-\frac{12}{5}\end{align*}$$
